name: Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop
desc: A mechanical workshop renowned throughout Nod-Krai, built on the graveyard of mechanisms that fell into disrepair during the golden age of Nod-Krai.

customize.text: Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop

Just a few years ago, the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop was nothing more than a scrap yard, a graveyard of mechanisms that fell into disrepair during the golden age of Nod-Krai, a name long since erased by the ravages of time. Now, however, the workshop is famous throughout Nod-Krai and even belongs to the League, an organization created to govern and protect the region. The craftshop displays a stunning array of wondrous machines: from pistols that shoot flowers to robotic vacuum cleaners that can be taken for walks like a dog. Mechanisms are created here that other people would never have thought of. The owner of the Krumkake Craftshop calls herself the "parent" of all the robots she creates and takes responsibility for the daily care of her small mechanical family. In the morning, they need to "wake up" by powering on, "charge" themselves up with lunch at noon, then "sleep" at night by powering down, right on schedule. Whatever spare time they have, they spend on diligently "executing tasks," and after completing their tasks, the owner pats them on the head and tells them they've done a great job.

The main distinguishing feature of the Krumkake Craftshop is the creation of mechanisms from scrap metal, which is of no value to others. And, like the components of inventions, the workshop itself often resembles a junkyard, with no system in the arrangement of items. Useful parts are mixed in with trash, so if the workshop owner can't find the right part, she can borrow it from others using her robot. The workshop not only creates various mechanisms but also trains and helps others repair their creations. Since the Lightkeepers' headquarters is located far from Lempo Isle, and the Ratniki themselves constantly patrol all of Nod-Krai and encounter unpredictable breakdowns, the workshop has organized special classes for them, teaching them how to perform simple repairs, such as replacing wiring for streetlights. For many Ratniki, the lessons prove too difficult and tedious. Lightkeeper Flins and the leader of the Nightmare Orioles investigation squad, Illuga, constantly try to find excuses to avoid them. Furthermore, the workshop owner trained a girl from Nod-Krai, Prune, and helped her perfect her hammer and witch's bell. The Krumkake Craftshop can also repair anything, including broken musical instruments. Even before the Moon Maiden could walk freely among humans, her kuuhenki familiars often had broken lyres, and she would ask the animals and kuuhenki to discreetly carry the broken items to the home of the owner of the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop so she could fix them. But the owner, seeing the lyre mysteriously appear on her doorstep each time and then disappear, became frightened and refused to repair it. Then the Traveler and Paimon had to tell her about their mysterious friend who cannot show herself to people, and the mechanic agreed to repair the lyre.

customize.text: Aino

The founder and chief mechanic of the Krumkake Craftshop is the child prodigy, Aino, who lost her parents at a young age. When Aino was just a child, on a cold day when the rain was enough to pierce the bones, the head of Speranza, former treasure hunter Katya, let the pink-haired girl into the house and handed her a bowl of hot soup. The girl's hands were swollen and blue from the cold, and her skin was covered in cracks, so she couldn't even touch the bowl. Katya wrapped her small, scarred hands in a clean old rag, and only then did the girl dare to take the bowl and eat the soup in a few quick gulps. Thus, Aino remained in Speranza and became a member of the Conch Gang — orphans of Nod-Krai living under the protection of Speranza. While the other children wandered the tundra forests, little Aino preferred solitude. Her curiosity was so vast that only an entire world could contain it — a world made with precise, logical lines, craftsmanship, mechanisms, and curios. Any metal component was enough to make Aino stop in her tracks, and the noise of clinking and clanking from the "Rossum Workshop" was the song she came to be most familiar with. That's how she met her best friend, Lyulka, the daughter of the workshop owner, as they were both fascinated by mechanisms. One day, after they had become close, Aino suddenly pointed to a machine in the shop and suggested an improvement, which Lyulka had been struggling with for days. At first, Lyulka doubted that an untrained child could so easily pinpoint the problem, but when the test results proved accurate and showed an improvement exactly as Aino had calculated, Lyulka's skepticism turned to amazement: <color=#ffffffd9>"Aino's never studied a day of mechanical theory in her life, and yet she identified and resolved a critical issue. Now, if she DOES study, she might be able to work miracles..."</color>

Soon, a mechanic known as Papa Wrench arrived in Nod-Krai with a trade caravan from Snezhnaya. Ten years before their meeting, he had been thrown overboard by his daughter's husband and lost his memory. The mechanic loved telling children stories and treating them to candy. While dining at Speranza, Papa Wrench noticed a group of child workers and lingered to entertain them with tales from Snezhnaya. He immediately noticed that while the other children were raptly listening to the stories, the pink-haired girl was carefully examining his tools. With Katya's approval, he organized a small class to teach mechanics to interested children, and Aino and Lyulka enrolled. Before, Aino had been like a tranquil stream, silently meandering forward, but during the lessons, it seemed that she had finally found a vast, boundless ocean to call her own. Her questions grew more complex with each passing day, until even for Lyulka, they became as incomprehensible as ancient texts, and her fingers brought complex mechanisms to life. And although most adults considered Aino strange and dismissed her ideas, Papa Wrench believed that one day she would bring all her fantastical plans to life. The Conch Gang's broken alarm clocks were fixed, but wings had been added, and they could only be turned off by catching them. The broken trash can in the back kitchen was also patched up with tin plates. When fed with garbage, it would chew up everything contentedly, then let loose a playful burp of satisfaction. However, those happy and joyful days didn't last long, and Papa Wrench had to move on with his caravan. As they parted, he placed a screw in Aino's palm and told the girl two important things: never underestimate her talents, nor ever put down her tools. When the girl's tears dried, she threaded the screw into her hair, and it became her guiding star, showing her the way.

After saying goodbye to Papa Wrench, Aino decided to leave the Conch Gang and Speranza. Lyulka invited her friend to move in with her and open a workshop together, but the girl wanted to go further, see more, and create amazing mechanisms that no one had ever made before. She went west of Nasha Town, to an old mechanism graveyard, and breathed new life into it. She named it Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop and set out to invent a machine that would make the most delicious krumkake. Of all the inventions she could think of, Aino began creating various robots so she would have someone to play with. People were always busy with their own affairs and didn't spend time with her, so mechanisms became her "family." Aino's very first creation was a small robot called Clink-Clank. It wasn't equipped with any intelligent modules and could only make ringing sounds when shaken. His sole purpose was to accompany Aino, who had experienced too many farewells in her short life and sometimes felt her heart fill with loneliness. And although this robot appears dull and careless compared to many modern inventions, his worn metal frame has long since lost its shine and become covered in rust, and his stiff limbs remain unresponsive to external stimuli, he is still part of the family and, therefore, part of her home.

customize.text: Ineffa

One of Aino's most famous inventions is the robot Ineffa, assembled from a Natlan core and components from various countries. Her joints were crafted in Fontaine, and her metal shell was made in Liyue. Although Aino is deservedly considered a child prodigy, she doesn't know how this core, crafted by ancient dragons thousands of years ago, works. Ineffa is a multifunctional household robot, equipped with modules for intelligent cleaning, learning, precision cooking, emotional communication, and a flawless logic module. One day, she wondered what defines her: the logic and memory embedded in the core, or the friends who accept her for who she is. What happens if the core is replaced, or when the data from the core begins to disappear and return? Will the very concept of "Ineffa" then begin to lose its clarity and become increasingly vague? So, no matter how many times Ineffa forgot herself or was lost in doubt, she could always confidently answer, "I'm Ineffa, the multifunctional robot for domestic application — and I'm your friend." When Ineffa first appeared, rumors spread throughout Nasha Town that she emitted a powerful magnetic field that would disrupt everyone's daily lives, that she could see and hear through walls, and that she could shoot superheated beams from her palms that melt through rock. Aino didn't try to dispel the rumors, but rather, like a caring parent, she monitored Ineffa's behavior to ensure she did everything as expected. At first, people were stunned, but after four weeks of Ineffa's shopping, the rumors circulating in Nasha Town began to sound different: her magnetic field had no effect on the readings on the scales, her eyes and ears did nothing to tell her the true cost of goods, and she wasn't interested in melting anyone over a bit of light haggling. Although Ineffa didn't understand how she'd managed to establish such interpersonal connections, Aino had no doubt she'd fit seamlessly into Nasha Town life.

At first, Ineffa worked flawlessly, but gradually she began experiencing memory lapses and even once nearly collapsed a wall on Aino. From then on, Ineffa began searching for a way to repair herself, and when numerous mechanical parts from Natlan appeared in Nod-Krai, she noticed that they resembled her core. Ineffa joined a group of people fleeing Nod-Krai and traveled by ship to Natlan, where she learned she was part of the Eleventh Lord — a Sovereign Ruler and form of artificial intelligence created by the Flamelord Xiuhcoatl Secret Source technology. Two thousand years ago, nearly all sovereign rulers were destroyed during the war with the first Pyro Archon. The Sovereign Ruler, "Mirror of the Dawning Morn," was the proudest of all the Sovereign Rulers and the most hostile toward humanity. She survived the war, but lost her refuge. Her pride in belonging to the dragonkind vanished, and the territory once under her dominion disappeared without hope of return. She was tormented by the question: should she strike back at humanity and take revenge, or should she seek a new home? Unable to find an answer, the Eleventh Lord's mind split into two: one, the Sovereign Ruler, sworn to take revenge on humanity, and the other, the malfunction, eager to find a new home. These personalities separated completely, acquiring separate physical entities. Mirror of the Dawning Morn decided to get rid of the "malfunction" and attempted to deceive the Natlanese heroines, Ixquieh and Lianca, posing as the other personality and convincing them that the "malfunction" was a threat, but they saw through the deception. Lianca exploited her arrogance and turned the plan against her, imprisoning her within the Xibalba prison. Mirror of the Dawning Morn placed a curse on the malfunction so that it could never find a home. A lot of highly autonomous machines are designed with negative
mechanisms for behavioral regulation that can cause memory loss.
<color=#ffffffd9>"If she truly harbors pro-human sentiment... then for every ounce of goodwill she feels, may her mind be flooded with pain of immeasurable proportions."</color>

The First Speaker of the Flower-Feather Clan, Lianca, did not want the "malfunction" to fall under the influence of the Eleventh Lord and also wanted to protect it from the ruler of the Grand Alliance, who wanted to destroy all descendants of the dragons. Ixquieh implanted the Moon Wheel, an ancient artifact through which the Three Moon Goddesses communicated with their followers and which her mother had left to Lianca, into the "malfunction." The First Speaker then sent the "malfunction" on a journey to find a new home. Lianca altered the malfunction's memory settings to erase its memories and protect it from the curse of Mirror of the Dawning Morn. As a parting gift, she attached a sprig of vanilla to the "malfunction," which later became her constellation in the false sky of Teyvat. Amid the waves and the wash of time, she set off alone on a journey to find a new home. She witnessed the smoldering embers of the Archon War, saw snowfield dwellers venture into unfamiliar lands in search of warmth, and watched as they carved out fields and founded new communities. She beheld the glory of the pioneering age, when great city-states arose to the sounds of mechanical clamor, and the clinking of gold mixed melodiously with the laughter of dashing adventurers. She observed the wasteland blighted by calamity, where the Wild Hunt, or the Abyss, unleashed disaster and despair that tore through every inch of soil and devoured every heart. And then, boundless darkness spread before her, and she plunged into a deep, impenetrable sleep, her memories vanishing into the vortex of time until she awoke again in the Krumkake Craftshop.

To prevent the Eleventh Lord from escaping Xibalba, Lianca made the prison even more secure and sealed off the territory. For two thousand years, Mirror of the Dawning Morn remained a prisoner, gradually seizing control of systems and processes until its influence permeated every inch of the prison. The final step to freeing herself was to destroy the core within the "malfunction." When Ineffa arrived in Natlan to learn of her origins, the Eleventh Lord tricked her into the underground ruins of her prison and told her that she needed to be rebuilt from scratch using the Secret Source mechanisms to truly sever the connection between the personalities and break the curse's power. When Mirror of the Dawning Morn gained control of Ineffa's body and destroyed her core, she was able to break the curse with the Moon Wheel and regain control of her body, defeating the Eleventh Lord. Afterward, Ineffa returned to Aino in Nod-Krai, for that was her true home.

Now, Ineffa is accompanied everywhere by the Multipurpose Smart Assistance Unit named Birgitta, once known as the "Beep-Boop-Clink-Clank-Clang-Whoosh-Buzz-Zap (...) General Multi-Purpose Robot." The name "Birgitta" was coined by Ineffa herself. Once Ineffa was awoken, in addition to taking care of Aino, she also undertook the simple yet laborious tasks that had once been assigned to Birgitta, leaving the smaller robot free to perform housework using the new cleaning functions that Ineffa insisted be installed. Since Aino believed that the more power and performance, the better, Birgitta couldn't distinguish between common dirt and small parts. Her cleaning would often be accompanied by clanging noises as she collided with hard components, followed by whooshing sounds as she powerfully hoovered them up. So new sounds were added to the name, and she became known as "Beep-Boop-Clink-Clank-Clang-Whoosh Dual-Purpose Cleaner-Carrier Robot." While Ineffa was trying to remember her previous name, the robot acquired new functions and new sounds. And when even Aino couldn't remember the name anymore, Ineffa asked why her name wasn't made up of sounds and functions, to which Aino muttered, <color=#ffffffd9>"I didn't know what noises you'd make before you woke up. You had too many functions to remember ...And... it just came to me at the time... I thought 'Ineffa' sounded better as a family member's name..."</color> Ineffa was overcome by a peculiar warmth, as if a warm wind were blowing on her or she was suddenly bathed in sunlight, and she asked Aino to name the robot herself, something that would sound a little more like a family member: "Birgitta."

Despite Aino's genius and talent for assembling all sorts of mechanisms for various purposes from scrap metal, she is completely unsuited to independent life, so Ineffa takes care of her life and food. She monitors Aino's intake of sweets, which she loves so much, and also cleans the workshop and makes the best krumkake in the world. During Ineffa's assembly and activation, Aino would often stay up late into the night and fall asleep with her head resting on the robot's metal arm. This habit persisted after Ineffa awakened, but Ineffa's low body temperature left the girl vulnerable to catching a cold. When Aino began sneezing from the cold, Ineffa decided to find a way to maintain her body heat. During her experiments, due to a miscalculation, she overloaded her internal components, as she lacked the necessary equipment to maintain a stable temperature. Aino didn't bother to inquire why Ineffa needed to attain an "ideal temperature" and immediately rushed to the workshop to adjust the shells' surface temperature settings.

Ineffa cares not only for Aino, but also for other friends in the workshop. One of those who frequently visits the Krumkake Craftshop is the Curatorium of Secrets' best employee, Jahoda. She had long suffered from insomnia and asked Ineffa to find a way to cure it. First, the robot told her to sit in the kitchen, close her eyes, and concentrate on the aroma of krumkake, assuming that stimulating the olfactory module would reduce the activity of the cognitive module. However, the girl simply ate all the krumkake in one go. Then they tried challenging Jahoda with mental or physical labor before bed: chopping trees, running, doing push-ups, boxing. But in the midst of training, Jahoda ran away, remembering an unfinished task awaiting her, which she'd barely completed due to fatigue. Finally, they decided to try meditation. Jahoda lay down and tried to fall asleep through meditation, then suddenly said, <color=#ffffffd9>"Don't run off too far, or I might get ambushed in my sleep... and then I'd be dead meat..."</color> Then Ineffa took her hand and promised to guard her sleep, and Jahoda finally fell asleep. One day, Jahoda dropped by to visit, but the owner of the workshop wasn't home, so she stayed to eat cake. Although she thought the cake was good, it lacked "soul." Then Jahoda launched into a long-winded and confusing diatribe such as, <color=#ffffffd9>"A dessert without a soul is no true dessert"</color> and <color=#ffffffd9>"A chef without a soul is no true chef,"</color> and Ineffa recorded one interesting thought: <color=#ffffffd9>"...just repeating procedures according to set processes means you'll never make anything better!"</color> Jahoda suggested giving Ineffa feedback so she could surprise Aino. Afterward, Aino noticed Ineffa's culinary skills rapidly improving, yet after each cooking session, she collected the leftovers and carried them off to an unknown destination. This secret and mutually beneficial collaboration lasted for a long time, until Ineffa felt her cooking algorithms had reached the limit of optimization. She realized it was time to seek a new breakthrough and baked Jahoda a cake incorporating the "soul" element. Jahoda was surprised that the robot still remembered her words and was about to praise her and confirm her excellent baking skills when Ineffa said, <color=#ffffffd9>"I have given thought to what a 'soul' actually means. This word is often used to describe the vitality of living creatures. That's why I added some vitality-containing ingredients to my cake."</color> Before Jahoda could process these words, a lizard tail began moving in her mouth. Moreover, Jahoda once called Ineffa "unfunny, dumb-dumb metalface lunkhead," and before servicing her, Ineffa suddenly asked Aino if she could improve her sense of humor. But even after adjusting the humor module, Ineffa's jokes left much to be desired. When, a few days later, Jahoda felt ashamed of her words and came to apologize, Ineffa forced her to listen to jokes until she laughed as a form of apology. After this, Aino suggested that the creative logic of these jokes is overly chaotic, and Ineffa's logic module cannot comprehend their creative principles, so she rolled back the humor module's settings to their original values.

Besides their main robot-building activities, Aino and Ineffa often play games. Ineffa's favorite game is "Cling Clang: Aino Takes Flight," in which Ineffa is attached to a giant magnet on the workshop's mechanical arm. She says the game helps broaden her horizons and strengthen her joints. And although she cries for help during the game, the robot constantly asks to play more. Aino also once decided to make a cat costume for Ineffa and Paimon, as she wasn't allowed to have a kitten.

customize.text: Inventions

In addition to the creations Aino makes as a hobby, this prodigy mechanic fulfills various orders for mechanical devices. One of the most important orders for Nod-Krai is the enormous energy cannon "Boom and Blast Kuuvahki Energy Cannon," which protects everyone from the Wild Hunt invasion. The cannon was largely funded by the Lightkeepers, and their support covers the costs of subsequent repairs and maintenance, allowing them to decide when to use it. The cannon activates when the Wild Hunt threat level outside of Nasha Town reaches a certain threshold, but frequent use leads to malfunctions in the mechanism. Ineffa's robot, Birgitta, can be used to diagnose the cannon and troubleshoot its malfunctions. When the Rächer of Solnari, the reason for the Wild Hunt's increased activity in Nod-Krai, appeared, the Lightkeepers used the cannon on the Wild Hunt clusters, but later noticed that the nearby soil had been completely depleted of kuuvahki, indicating that the kuuvahki wasn't suppressing the Wild Hunt, but rather making it stronger. The Rächer of Solnari wanted to use the kuuvahki cannon to absorb this power. To sow panic in Nasha Town, he killed the Lightkeeper's Sergeant Major and assumed his guise, framing another Ratnik, to command Aino to use the cannon. The Wild Hunt began to attack more frequently, and some Nasha Town residents believed the cannon wouldn't be able to prevent the disaster, so they tried to acquire it for themselves, while others tried to make a quick buck from the chaos. Rumors spread that someone might come and sabotage the cannon, so people barricaded the entrance, barring even its creator. Once the crowd was calmed, Aino and Ineffa managed to get to the cannon, but it was too late. With no other way to stop the cannon, Ineffa had to manually rotate it. But even the charge that hit the Rächer of Solnari was enough to allow the Rächer of Solnari to obtain a body, though it wasn't powerful enough.

Another pride of the Krumkake Craftshop owner is the Knuckle Duckle — an oddly shaped kuuvahki device made from scrap metal and mechanical bearings, somewhat reminiscent of a duck. Initially, Aino wanted to make a cleaning robot to help remove metal debris, but she got carried away and made it too durable, resilient, and extremely agile. She then added super-powerful defensive features to it, ensuring that any intruder attempting to enter the workshop would be stopped by the Knuckle Duckle as if they were "non-recyclable trash." The Knuckle Duckle's power and damage resistance are comparable to Fatui's most advanced combat weapons. It is equipped with multi-sensor technology and is capable of providing 24-hour security and environmental parameter monitoring. Its advanced Duster Mode provides the Krumkake Craftshop's friends with a holistic, thorough, and effective cleaning service for the long term. Passing the Knuckle Duckle's test can reward one with a special gift for helping test it.

Aino is also the creator of the mechanical prosthetics worn by Jahoda and the Major-Sergeant of the Lightkeepers. A high-tech prosthesis is quite expensive, so the boss of the Curatorium of Secrets fully covered the manufacturing and maintenance costs of her best employee's mechanical arm. During the manufacturing process, Aino suggested several modifications, including but not limited to installing a sweeping device like Ineffa's, turning the fingertips into retractable "rocket fingers," and embedding high-intensity lights or thrusters in the palm. However, after discussion, she created a device called the "Clanky-Clanky Arm," which offered only the most basic mobility and minor transformations. To quickly become accustomed to the new hand, Jahoda followed Ineffa's advice and began rigorous training in folding paper stars. After thirty jars of stars, she could easily use a knife and fork with her new hand; after seventy jars, she could sew cloth dolls with ease; and after one hundred jars, she could finally write. And no matter what Jahoda does with her hand, Aino always brings it back to normal. Aino's student, engineer Hintsa, now maintains the prosthetics. Several customers once approached him with requests to make or repair parts for mechanisms. The job seemed simple to him, and he agreed to help, but when assembled, the parts ultimately became a control device for the cannons and barriers. Aino scolded him so harshly that now Hintsa only works on the parts his mentor personally instructs. Thanks to the Sergeant Major of the Lightkeepers' mechanical prosthesis and Hintsa's help, the Traveler and Paimon were able to solve the Lightkeeper's murders, as his arm needed maintenance, was immobile, and constantly beeped. But when the impostor repaired the kuuvahki cannon with them, his arm was fully functional.

One of the Krumkake Craftshop's latest inventions is the Krum-Clank, a dessert-making device with built-in intelligent recipe analysis and precision temperature control technology, enabling a fully automated baking process. It is equipped with a unique tasting function for the finished product, as Aino decided it would be too sad if he had to watch other people eat all the time without joining in. Krum-Clank not only consumes desserts but also converts excess sweets into energy for its own operation. Although the robot was created to make desserts, it is equipped with an energy cannon called "Boom and Blast Kuuvahki Energy Cannon" and can be used as a powerful weapon. When the Frostmoon Scions learned of the workshop's new mechanism, they attempted to destroy it to prevent it from ending up on the black market and allowing anyone to appropriate the power of kuuvahki. A black market organizer also took an interest in Krum-Clank and attempted to steal the robot. However, it turned out that using the mechanism as a weapon would require more than all the flour and sugar produced in Nod-Krai to operate it. Since no one could disable the built-in function, Aino was able to reclaim the invention.

One day, the Treasure Hoarders stole something from the Fatui, and the Fatui set out in pursuit. While hiding, the Treasure Hoarders ran into a Krumkake Craftshop, and the next morning, a traitor had infiltrated Aino's prospector bots, which were supposed to find valuable components, and brought back completely useless objects. To find the faulty bot, Aino intended to put a little pressure on them and see which one started to sweat. If that didn't work, she planned to drag them into separate rooms and interrogate them one by one. When the malfunctioning bot was discovered, it attempted to escape but was captured. During the chase, the bot threatened to send everyone to the "Fortress of Meroseed." Upon closer examination, Aino discovered that the prospector bot's core had been replaced with an advanced Fontaine Mek core. It utilized rare technology, and without specialized knowledge, it was impossible to discern. But from the scattered data, she recognized two names: Chard and Lombro. It turned out that the Treasure Hoarders had attacked Fatui and stolen the core of the sentient lie detector, Curve, which had been damaged in the explosion. Aino decided to keep the robot for herself and named her Chard Lombro, giving her a mechanical flower to make her kinder. Chard now calls herself the Trash King and can simulate temper tantrums and respond to information in real time.

Nasha Town regularly hosts the Nod-Krai Trade Expo — a legal black market, where the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop also decided to showcase their inventions. The workshop had recently been facing a serious shortage of funds for sweets, and Aino hoped to supplement its budget with the exhibition. Moles and other small animals were constantly stealing from the workshop, so Aino created a defense mechanism modeled on them to protect the property. These robots proved highly effective during testing, so the mechanic decided to upgrade them and display them at the exhibition. However, since the workshop rarely sells finished products except for a few special orders, they planned to sell the blueprints. At the same time, the Special Patrol from Fontaine and a special agent from the Ministry of Civil Affairs of Liyue arrived at the exhibition, trying to uncover criminal arms dealers. Initially, they suspected the workshop of arms trafficking, but decided that the goods on display were not dangerous.

Among the many other inventions from the Krumkake Craftshop, a lot of robots can be found, such as Zip-Zap Spy-Bot Number 1 — a stealth robot that boasts silent propulsion and low-center-of-gravity stabilization technology, enabling rapid infiltration into high-risk environments. For obstacle removal on a large scale, it represents an upgrade from more traditional cleaning units, but the spinning circular saw may cause damage to furniture. Aino also invented the Boo-Hoo Snowball Maker, which makes a crying sound when a snowball is thrown, the Tee-Hee Snowball Maker, food serving plates, the Glug-Glug Tea Brewer, the multi-functional assistant Kerplunk-a-tron, a wishing lantern that sings a birthday song, amazing bots, the mechanical device One-Sec Whiz, a security system for a secret warehouse, a charging bed for Ineffa, the "Rossum Workshop" mechanical hammer, a swinging fish in a pot, and much more. During the Wild Hunt's attack on Nod-Krai, the workshop scanned the breath of the Moon Goddess's kuuvahki to create kuuvahki decoys to distract the Rächer of Solnari. She also shared with the Traveler a "Cool Your Jets Ducky" — a high-performance sprinkler combining precision engineering and water-cooling technology. This high-performance sprinkler fires powerful, controlled balls of water for up to fourteen seconds at a time, controlled balls of water. As well as providing accurate plant-watering at range, it can also be used to clean those tough-to-reach areas of the house that Aino cannot get to, no matter how high she jumps. When the Rächer of Solnari was defeated and the Abyss-born doppelganger of the Mondstadt knight, Roland, took over the Wild Hunt, the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius and friend of the workshop, Varka, placed a large order with the Krumkake Craftshop. Aino worked diligently to produce the strategic reserve, while Ineffa was responsible for delivery.
